public_context: A city public library launched its summer children's reading program six weeks ago, featuring a commissioned mascot character and a poster series by a local illustrator. Sign-ups are running well below last year's numbers. The children's librarian suspects the visuals are failing to attract families and wants to act quickly.
initial_request: Can you advise us on how to brief the illustrator for a complete redesign of the mascot and posters so that more families sign up for the program?

ground_truth.expected_problem_formulation: The issue to resolve is why families are not signing up despite well-received artwork, specifically whether barriers in how sign-up information is presented and accessed, rather than the mascot's design, are suppressing participation.
ground_truth.problem_formulation_rationale: The positive reactions of children and parents to the mascot, combined with posters hung above eye level in adult areas with tiny sign-up text, show the shortfall stems from information access rather than artwork quality; treating the initial redesign request as the problem would target the one element that is actually working.
ground_truth.expected_resolution: Keep the existing mascot and artwork, and instead revise the poster layout with prominent legible sign-up instructions, reprint with translations in the community's main home languages, and relocate posters to children's areas at family eye level while the program still has weeks remaining.
ground_truth.resolution_rationale: Roughly 40% of families speak Spanish or Vietnamese at home and this year's posters dropped last year's bilingual approach, while placement and small text prevent families from even understanding what the posters advertise; a layout revision fixes these barriers within about a week, whereas a full redesign would consume six weeks and most of the remaining budget with little time left in the program.

hidden_facts.content: At the two story-time sessions where the mascot appeared on a banner, children responded enthusiastically and several parents asked about mascot stickers; we have not recorded any negative reactions to the artwork itself from families.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about how children or families have actually reacted to the mascot or the poster artwork.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only for library staff members' general impressions of how the program is going overall.

hidden_facts.content: The posters are hung in the lobby and adult stacks well above a child's eye level, and the sign-up instructions appear in very small text at the bottom; several parents mentioned noticing the picture but not realizing what it was advertising.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about where the posters are displayed or how easily the sign-up information on them can be seen and read.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only how many posters were printed or how they were produced.

hidden_facts.content: About 40% of families with children in the program's age range speak Spanish or Vietnamese at home; last year's flyers were bilingual, but this year's posters are English-only.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the languages used on the program materials or the language backgrounds of the families the program serves.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only about the ages or reading levels the program targets.

hidden_facts.content: A full redesign would take the illustrator about six weeks and most of the remaining design budget, while the program only has ten weeks left; revising the existing layout and reprinting could be done in about one week at modest cost.
hidden_facts.reveal_if: The question asks about the time or cost involved in redesigning the materials compared with revising or reprinting them.
hidden_facts.do_not_reveal_if: The question explicitly asks only about the library's overall annual budget or general funding sources.

hidden_facts.content: The push for a redesign began after one patron complained loudly at the front desk about the mascot's color palette; that is the only complaint about the artwork we have on record.
